tagline.text: A fishing town southeast of Mactan with mangroves and the Gilutongan marine sanctuary

location.label: Location
location.text: Cordova, southeastern Mactan Island (about 28 km from Cebu City)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–5,000 (per person, boat, meals and transport included)

children.text: Cordova is a fishing municipality at the southeastern tip of Mactan Island, known for about 100 hectares of mangrove forest and the marine sanctuaries of Gilutongan and Nalusuan islands. It is close to the airport, and the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway, opened in 2022, has made it easy to reach from Cebu City too.
Cordova lies on the southeastern side of Mactan Island, about
28 km
from Cebu City and about
18 km

from Lapu-Lapu City. It has 13 barangays and about 73,000 residents (2024 census); the most populous barangay is Ibabao (about 10,000). It is an unusual place: a densely populated fishing suburb that also holds marine sanctuaries.

Cordova was created on May 22, 1863, when Spanish Governor-General Rafael Echagüe combined the villages of Gabi, Day-as and Pilipul (now Pilipog); the decree took effect in 1864. The name is presumed to come from Córdoba in Spain, though this is not certain. It is linked to the rest of Mactan by two bridges, and Mactan in turn connects to mainland Cebu by two bridges between Mandaue and Lapu-Lapu City. Today Cordova is known as one of the places on Mactan Island that retains the most fishing-town character.

Cordova became important to travelers thanks to the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX), completed in 2022. Because the expressway connects Cebu City and Cordova directly, you can arrive much faster than before. It is also close to the airport, so it is a good half-day stop when you have time before a flight. Toll fees and traffic vary from day to day, so check a map app before you set out. If you are transiting through the airport, decide first whether you can leave your bags and how you will time your return.

Cordova's appeal is nature experiences. About 100 hectares of mangrove forest spread across Pilipog, Bangbang, San Miguel, Day-as and Catarman, and the Day-as Boardwalk and Marine Park is the best place to reach it. Out to sea, the Gilutongan and Nalusuan island marine sanctuaries in the Olango Island Group offer snorkeling and diving. Cordova is not a place with big nightlife or shopping, but a quiet fishing municipality. It suits a one-day visit to see the sanctuaries and mangroves and return, or a half-day stop while staying at a resort on Mactan. Combined with other sights on Mactan, it makes a full itinerary. If you have a long wait before your flight, spend the time with a nature experience in this municipality near the airport.

Gilutongan Island, part of the Olango Island Group, is known as a marine sanctuary that protects coral reefs and tropical fish. You go by boat and snorkel; check entrance and sanctuary fees on site. Wear a life jacket, follow the sanctuary staff's guidance, and do not feed fish or touch coral. Visibility and currents change day to day, so ask the boat operator about conditions on the day you go.
Nalusuan Island has both a resort and a marine sanctuary. It is known as a snorkeling spot; ask the resort about lodging and activity prices.

A wooden walkway that lets you walk over the mangrove forest. It is the easiest access to the roughly 100 hectares of mangroves, where you can watch birds, crabs and small fish. The walkway is near the sea, but the bottom can be muddy depending on the tide, so non-slip shoes are recommended. A hat and water are essential in the hot midday sun.

The mangrove forest across the barangays of Pilipog, Bangbang, San Miguel, Day-as and Catarman protects the coast and serves as a spawning ground for fish. Follow the designated paths when walking. Mangroves reduce the waves of tropical storms and store carbon, so their conservation value is high. Take your trash with you when you visit.

Described as a public beach visited by many local families. Water color and facilities differ from place to place, so check when you arrive. On weekends it is crowded with families, and weekday mornings are quiet. Check the swimming area and depth, and watch children.
A beach resort in Cordova listed by Wikipedia. Room and facility prices vary by season, so check booking sites and official information. It is close to the airport and suits a short rest.

A cafe and a leisure spot that Wikipedia lists as places worth visiting in Cordova. Opening hours, entry arrangements and menus can change, so check recent reviews or official accounts before you go. They make a pleasant break between beach and mangrove plans.

Cordova is still a village where fishing is alive. If you go to a landing early in the morning, you can see bangka boats and the fish market. The fishing villagers make a living from boats and fishing, so ask permission before taking photos.

items.title: From Cebu City via the CCLEX

children.text: Cebu City and Cordova are directly connected by the Cebu–Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX), completed in 2022.
Travel by taxi, Grab or rental car. Check tolls locally.
From the airport to Cordova is within the same island of Mactan, quoted at around
30 minutes to 1 hour
depending on road conditions. It varies greatly with traffic.
Jeepneys and vans run between Mactan and Cordova. Check routes locally.
Between town and the landing, use a tricycle or habal-habal.
For Gilutongan and Nalusuan islands, arrange a boat at the landing. Negotiate and check the safety equipment.
Boats are generally arranged at the local landing shortly before departure, and going early in high season gives you more choice.
The dry season from December to May is best for snorkeling and getting to the islands. The sea is calm and visibility is clear.
In the rainy season waves get higher and boats may be canceled. If a typhoon is forecast, cancel your island plans.
The look of the mangroves and shallow sea differs with the tide. At high tide the water is full and good for walking; at low tide the bottom is exposed and shows a different scene.

Consider both the resorts on Cordova's coast and hotels on Mactan Island. Being near the airport, it is a good place to stay a night before a connection or just after arrival.

Grilled fish, shrimp and squid at restaurants near the landing are the basics, and there are a few cafes too. On weekends many local families visit. Seafood prices vary with the market, so check the weight and unit price before ordering.
There are few restaurants on the islands, so bring water and snacks before boarding the boat.

When staying in Cordova, compare the locations of beach resorts and Mactan hotels, whether breakfast is included and the travel time to the airport. Some restaurants near the landing have no price list, so it is safer to confirm prices before ordering.
Confirm the total boat price, the time and the number of islands before you set out.
When snorkeling, do not step on or touch coral, and use reef-friendly sunscreen.
Wear a life jacket and put electronics in a waterproof pouch.
The mangrove walkway is cool in the morning. Bring mosquito repellent.
Bring plenty of cash. Many places at the islands and landing do not take cards.
Because it is close to the airport, it works well as a half-day trip if you have a long layover.
Check the latest information on island fees and schedules.
Even though it is close to the airport, allow at least half a day for the boat trip.
If you have an underwater camera or waterproof case, you can take good snorkeling photos.
In the rainy and typhoon seasons, sea conditions can change suddenly and make boats dangerous, so check the weather forecast and do not set out recklessly.
Coral collecting, feeding fish and fishing are restricted in the sanctuaries.
Some beaches have no lifeguards, so check the swimming area.
Small boats have limits on luggage and passengers, so keep to the capacity.
Fees and rules change, so check with the municipal office and the sanctuary offices.
Check the freshness and price of seafood, and if you are trying it for the first time, watch for allergies.
